title: A Tale of Valour: Major Somnath Sharma and the Battle of Badgam

topics.title: Major Somnath Sharma: the first Param Vir Chakra

learn.hook: India's highest award for bravery has a very special first name on its list. Whose is it, and what did he do?
points: The lesson is a true account of courage: how Major Somnath Sharma led his soldiers in the Battle of Badgam.
The Param Vir Chakra (PVC) is India's highest military award for gallantry, given for the greatest bravery in the face of the enemy.
Major Somnath Sharma of the 4th Battalion of the Kumaon Regiment was the first-ever recipient of the Param Vir Chakra.

The Battle of Badgam was fought on 3 November 1947, near Srinagar in Jammu and Kashmir. His company held its position against a much larger attacking force until more troops arrived, helping to protect the Srinagar airfield.
He gave his life in this battle, so he received the award posthumously, which means after his death.

example.q: Read this original tribute: 'His arm was in a plaster cast, yet he would not stay behind. At Badgam he moved from post to post, cheering his men and guiding them, and he did not leave his position.' Think it through: what does this tell us about his character?
steps: Notice the injury: his arm was in a plaster cast.
Notice what he did anyway: he went with his men and moved from post to post.
Notice how he treated his soldiers: he cheered and guided them.
Put it together: he was brave, dutiful and a caring leader.
example.answer: He was courageous and devoted to duty, and he led and encouraged his men even when he was injured.

learn.reallife: The National War Memorial in New Delhi honours India's brave soldiers, including Param Vir Chakra recipients like Major Somnath Sharma.

games.title: Timeline
games.prompt: Put these events in the order they happened

games.title: Facts about a hero
items: Major Somnath Sharma was the first person to receive the Param Vir Chakra.
His name is the first in the list of Param Vir Chakra recipients.
The Param Vir Chakra is an award for excellence in sports.
It is India's highest military award for gallantry.
The Battle of Badgam took place in 1947.
Major Somnath Sharma received the award posthumously.
He gave his life in the battle, so the award was given after his death.
Major Somnath Sharma served in the Indian Navy.
He was an officer of the Indian Army, in the Kumaon Regiment.
The battle helped protect the Srinagar airfield nearby.

quiz.q: The Param Vir Chakra is ___.
options: India's highest military award for gallantry
quiz.explain: The PVC is the highest gallantry award of India's armed forces, for bravery in the face of the enemy.
quiz.mistake: Confuses military gallantry awards with other national awards

quiz.q: Who was the first recipient of the Param Vir Chakra?
quiz.explain: Major Somnath Sharma was the first. Captain Vikram Batra also received the PVC, but in 1999.
quiz.mistake: Picks another famous name linked with the army

quiz.q: The Battle of Badgam was fought on ___.
quiz.explain: The battle took place on 3 November 1947, a few months after Independence.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the battle date with Independence Day or Republic Day

quiz.q: 'He was awarded the medal posthumously.' Here 'posthumously' means ___.
quiz.explain: 'Posthumous' means happening after a person's death.
quiz.mistake: Links 'post' with the postal service

quiz.q: Major Somnath Sharma belonged to which regiment?
quiz.explain: He was an officer of the 4th Battalion of the Kumaon Regiment (4 Kumaon).
quiz.mistake: Guesses a well-known regiment without recalling the fact

quiz.q: Read: 'Though his arm was in plaster, he moved from post to post, cheering his men.' What does this tell us?
options: He was afraid of the battle
He was injured but still led his men bravely
He stayed back at the base
quiz.explain: 'Though' shows contrast: even with an injured arm, he kept leading and encouraging his soldiers.
quiz.mistake: Misses the contrast word 'though'

quiz.q: Badgam is in which present-day Union Territory of India?
quiz.explain: Badgam (also spelt Budgam) is near Srinagar in Jammu and Kashmir.
quiz.mistake: Picks a nearby hilly region

quiz.q: Which word means 'great courage, especially in battle'?
quiz.explain: 'Valour' means great bravery, as in the chapter title 'A Tale of Valour'.
quiz.mistake: Confuses valour with the similar-looking word 'value'

teach.ask: Gappu salutes with one wing: Who was Major Somnath Sharma, and why is he remembered?
teach.praise: Jai Hind! He was the first Param Vir Chakra recipient, for his courage at Badgam in 1947.
teach.nudge: Which award did he receive first of all? Where and when was the battle? What quality did he show?

learn.hook: You cannot hold courage in your hand, put it in your bag or weigh it. So what kind of noun is it?
points: Words close in meaning to courage: bravery, valour, gallantry, heroism, fearlessness. Opposites: cowardice, timidity, fearfulness.
An abstract noun names a quality, feeling or idea that we cannot see or touch: courage, honesty, freedom, kindness, loyalty.
Many abstract nouns come from adjectives: brave → bravery, loyal → loyalty, strong → strength, proud → pride, wise → wisdom, free → freedom, kind → kindness.
Some come from common nouns or verbs: hero → heroism, friend → friendship and decide → decision.
Courage is not only for soldiers. Telling the truth, standing up for someone who is being teased, or trying again after failing also takes courage.

example.q: Think it through: Find the abstract nouns in this sentence: 'The soldier's bravery and loyalty earned the respect of the whole nation.'
steps: Check each noun: soldier, bravery, loyalty, respect, nation.
A soldier and a nation can be seen, so they are not abstract.
Bravery, loyalty and respect are qualities or feelings that cannot be touched.

learn.reallife: The Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Bal Puraskar honours children for achievements that include bravery, such as saving someone in danger.

quiz.q: Which word is a synonym of 'courage'?
quiz.explain: Bravery and courage both mean facing danger or difficulty without giving in to fear.
quiz.mistake: Picks the antonym 'cowardice'

quiz.q: Which word is the antonym of 'brave'?
quiz.explain: Cowardly means lacking courage, the opposite of brave. The other words are synonyms.
quiz.mistake: Picks a synonym instead of an antonym

quiz.q: What is the abstract noun formed from 'strong'?
quiz.explain: Strong (adjective) → strength (abstract noun). 'Strongly' is an adverb and 'stronger' is a comparative.
quiz.mistake: Adds '-ness' or '-ly' without knowing the correct form

quiz.q: Which of these is an abstract noun?
quiz.explain: Honesty is a quality that cannot be seen or touched. The others are things or people you can see.
quiz.mistake: Thinks important words like 'medal' are abstract

quiz.q: Choose the correct word: The firefighter was praised for his ___.
quiz.explain: After 'his' we need a noun, and the noun form is 'bravery'.
quiz.mistake: Uses the adjective where a noun is needed

quiz.q: What does 'gallantry' mean in 'an award for gallantry'?
quiz.explain: Gallantry awards honour great bravery, especially in battle or danger.
quiz.mistake: Confuses 'gallantry' with 'gallery'

quiz.q: Which sentence shows everyday courage?
options: Asha told the truth even though she feared being scolded.
quiz.explain: Telling the truth when you are afraid of the result takes courage.
quiz.mistake: Thinks courage only means fighting

quiz.q: What is the abstract noun formed from 'hero'?
quiz.explain: Heroism is the quality of being a hero. 'Heroic' is an adjective and 'heroes' is a plural.
quiz.mistake: Picks the adjective or the plural form

teach.ask: Gappu tries to pick up 'courage' with his beak and fails. What is an abstract noun? Give me some examples!
teach.praise: Aha! Abstract nouns name qualities like bravery and honesty that we can't touch, only feel or show.
teach.nudge: Can you see or touch 'courage'? What kind of things do abstract nouns name? Give me an example.

topics.title: Telling a true story: past tenses

learn.hook: A true story already happened. To tell it clearly, you need the right past tense at the right moment.
points: Simple past tells a completed action at a definite time: The battle began at dawn. We watched the parade yesterday.
Past continuous (was/were + verb-ing) shows an action in progress in the past: The soldiers were guarding the airfield.
Past continuous + simple past shows a longer action interrupted by a shorter one: We were eating dinner when the lights went off.
Past perfect (had + past participle) shows an action completed before another past action: The film had started when we reached the hall.
Learn irregular verbs: fight-fought-fought, hold-held-held, lead-led-led, give-gave-given, win-won-won, write-wrote-written.

example.q: Think it through: Join these two sentences using the past perfect. 'The match finished. Then we reached the stadium.'
steps: Find the earlier action: the match finished.
The earlier action takes the past perfect: had finished.
The later action stays in simple past: reached.
example.answer: The match had finished when we reached the stadium.

learn.reallife: Diaries, news reports and history books use past tenses to tell what happened, what was happening, and what had already happened.

items.text: Yesterday we ___ the Republic Day parade on TV.
The children ___ playing when the bell rang.
By the time we arrived, the show ___ started.
Our team ___ the kabaddi final last year.
The captain ___ his team bravely in the final.

quiz.q: Which sentence is in the past continuous tense?
quiz.explain: Was + writing (verb-ing) shows an action in progress in the past.
quiz.mistake: Confuses past continuous with simple past or past perfect

quiz.q: Choose the correct option: The film ___ when we reached the hall.
quiz.explain: The film started before we reached, so the earlier action takes the past perfect 'had started'.
quiz.mistake: Uses present perfect in a past story

quiz.q: What is the past tense of 'lead'?
quiz.explain: 'Lead' is irregular: lead-led-led.
quiz.mistake: Adds '-ed' to an irregular verb

quiz.q: 'They were digging the garden when the rain began.' Which action was already in progress?
quiz.explain: 'Were digging' is past continuous, a longer action that the rain interrupted.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the simple past action was the longer one

quiz.q: Which tense shows an action completed before another past action?
quiz.explain: The past perfect (had + past participle) marks the earlier of two past actions.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the past continuous shows the earlier action

quiz.q: Fill in the blank: Yesterday, the students ___ the national flag at dawn.
quiz.explain: 'Yesterday' is a definite past time, so the simple past 'hoisted' is correct.
quiz.mistake: Uses the present perfect with a definite past time

quiz.q: Choose the correct option: While I ___ my homework, the lights went off.
quiz.explain: Homework was in progress when a shorter action interrupted it, so use past continuous.
quiz.mistake: Uses simple past for the longer, interrupted action

quiz.q: What is the past participle of 'give'?
quiz.explain: give-gave-given. 'Gave' is the simple past; 'given' is the past participle, used with 'had' or 'has'.
quiz.mistake: Uses the simple past form where the past participle is needed

teach.ask: Gappu scratches his head: When do I say 'was flying' and when do I say 'had flown'?
teach.praise: Chirp! 'Was flying' is past continuous for something going on, and 'had flown' is past perfect for something done before another past action.
teach.nudge: Which helping verb shows an action in progress? Which helping verb shows an action that happened earlier?
